thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 detected: sustained 5xx spike on /v1/generate and /v1/chat for hosted region us-west-2. Symptoms: increasing token latency and KV cache key explosion. Pager triggered at 09:12 UTC :rotating_light:

maria (eng-runtime): saw the alert, looking now. initial hypothesis = batch key churn after yesterday's tokenizer tweak? :thinking_face:

sanjay (oncall): I'm on it. current impact: ~12% p50 latency regression and 10% request 500s over last 15m, errors mostly from runtime cache eviction OOMs. Can someone share last deploy diff?

eli (eng-ml): quick note — we rolled tokenizer normalization change in model-service:fc-20260314 at 02:30 UTC (small whitespace normalization). Could be related to prompt hashing.

maria (eng-runtime): that matches. If tokenizer output changes, prefix hash keys change -> KV prefix cache can't dedupe and we end up creating millions of tiny entries which thrashes memory.

jen (support): Tina from support reports two paying customers seeing timeouts on multi-turn chat flows. They reported increased errors just after 09:00 UTC. Customer IDs: acct-9843, acct-1102. Tina: any more details?

tina (cs): customers seeing 504s on long context prompts, they said recent prompt templates (same app) used to be fine. Escalated and they're asking for ETA. They are currently in-prod.

lee (eng-sre): I'm pulling OOM traces now. Heap profile shows a 22x increase in live KV keys with prefix length 128-256. Also seeing lots of small allocations from prefix-hash entries.

ops-bot: deploy fc-20260314 triggered at 02:31 UTC by ci/cd pipeline (author: eli (eng-ml)).

maria (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation option: 1) disable continuous batching for affected pool(s) (cheap stopgap), 2) backfill prefix-hash normalization to previous behavior, 3) evict small keys by TTL sweep. I can push a config change to reduce batch window to 10ms and max batch tokens to 256. Want to avoid full rollback if possible.

sanjay (oncall): do step 1 now (reduce batching) and schedule a TTL sweep. If that doesn't drop key growth in 10m, we'll rollback deploy. I'll take ownership for the next 30m then handoff.

maria (eng-runtime): applying 10ms batch window patch to prod us-west-2 pools now. patch command:

```bash
# reduce continuous batching window
redwoodctl config set pool.us-west-2.batch.window_ms 10
redwoodctl config set pool.us-west-2.batch.max_tokens 256
```

maria (eng-runtime): patch applied at 09:20 UTC. ops-bot shows config apply OK.

lee (eng-sre): running TTL sweep job now (ttl=30s for small prefixes). Job id: ttl-sweep-1819999999. Kickoff logs:

```
[09:21:10] scanned 3.1M prefixes, evicted 2.8M small entries
[09:21:35] reclaimed ~4.2GB memory
```

lee (eng-sre): memory pressure falling, live KV count down by ~70% in 6m. Latency downstream improving. :thumbsup:

jen (support): updated customers with temporary mitigation and ETA ~30m for stability. They asked if we can prevent recurrence.

eli (eng-ml): root cause analysis initial: tokenizer normalization introduced different token boundaries for templates containing narrow non-breaking spaces and zero-width spaces. That changed the canonical prompt string used by prompt-hash, generating many unique prefixes. I reproduced locally with sample template: 

```python
orig = "Hello\u00A0World"
new = normalize_tokenizer(orig)  # stripped & resegmented
# prompt_hash(orig) != prompt_hash(new)
```

maria (eng-runtime): confirmed. prompt-hash function used raw token bytes from tokenizer output, no stable normalization. So tokenizer change = hash divergence.

lee (eng-sre): current status summary for handoff at 09:30 UTC: batching narrowed, TTL sweep reclaimed memory, 5xx rate back to baseline but p50 still slightly elevated. No customer-facing incidents open besides followups from Tina. Next steps: patch prompt-hash to normalize token stream OR revert tokenizer change in service. We need decision from eng/ML on safe path.

eli (eng-ml): preference: roll tokenizer change back for now (low-risk revert), then roll-forward with a migration that preserves canonicalization invariants. I can cut the revert PR now.

maria (eng-runtime): agree. Reverting will restore hash stability quickly. I'll prepare the rollback plan and coordinate canary.

sanjay (oncall): I'm handing off to lee (eng-sre) for the next shift. Hand-off note: watch mem and 5xx for 30m after rollback. If key growth resumes, escalate to SEV1.

sanjay (oncall): handoff to lee at 09:33 UTC. 

lee (eng-sre): ack. I'll run the rollback if we don't see continued improvement. Can someone post the rollback PR link and the exact commit id to revert?

eli (eng-ml): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-service/pull/4523 revert fc-20260314 (commit: a1b2c3d4). I will attach a short migration doc in the PR for follow-up.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll coordinate canary steps after revert is ready. Canary plan: roll to 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 5m, measure KV key delta and p50, then 25% for 10m, then full. Rollback script:

```bash
# rollback model-service to previous deploy
deployctl rollback model-service --to-commit a1b2c3d4 --staged=true --region us-west-2
# monitor
watch "redwoodctl metrics get region.us-west-2.kv.live_keys"
```

lee (eng-sre): good. I'll keep TTL sweep running at low cadence (every 2m) until rollback is complete.

maria (eng-runtime): ops-bot: create incident ticket INC-2026-00078 with summary "prefix hash churn after tokenizer normalization" and add oncall, eng-runtime, eng-ml, support. Include customers acct-9843/1102.

ops-bot: INC-2026-00078 created. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-00078

tina (cs): customers acknowledged receipt. They asked for a postmortem and ETA for a permanent fix.

eli (eng-ml): I'll open a follow-up task for migration: ensure prompt-hash uses normalized canonical form and add property tests for tokenizer/hashing invariants.

maria (eng-runtime): follow-up action items: 1) short-term: rollback tokenizer in model-service (eli) + TTL sweeps (lee) + monitor (maria). 2) medium-term: harden prompt-hash to be resilient to tokenizer normalization changes (maria + eli). 3) add canary/perf test that simulates template-driven prefix distributions (eng-runtime + eng-ml).

lee (eng-sre): update at 09:56 UTC: p50 back to baseline after TTL sweep and config change. Rolling back tokenizer now (eli).

eli (eng-ml): rollback started at 09:59 UTC. Canary at 5% passing. Monitoring keys + p50.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks team. I'll draft the initial incident notes for postmortem and link to the PR and INC ticket.

jen (support): I'll keep customers updated and schedule a follow-up call with acct-9843 tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigation in progress, severity downgraded to SEV3. Next update in 30m or on major change.

lee (eng-sre): leaving oncall at 10:20 UTC, handoff to sanjay (oncall) with note: monitor keys, confirm rollback finishes, confirm customers stable.

sanjay (oncall): ack handoff.

maria (eng-runtime): final note: root cause = tokenizer normalization subtle change -> prompt_hash invariant broken. Long-term fix: canonicalize at hashing boundary and add regression tests. We'll include evals to detect key explosion patterns in canaries.

--- end of thread ---
